intro: Respiratory therapists combine patient care with technical equipment skills. The closest of the 25 careers below is cardiovascular technology, with a 92% skill match, while Nuclear Medicine Technologists are 81% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $101,370, which is 23% more than the $82,280 respiratory therapists earn.
why_it_works: Treating patients with breathing problems means running ventilators, reading results and calming people who are struggling to breathe. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and service orientation at 3.75. Imaging, nuclear medicine and cardiovascular roles use the same mix of patient and equipment skills. Almost every match needs no new degree, though most need their own certification.
tips: MRI technologists earn $95,480, which is 16% more, and many programs accept respiratory therapists.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, or 79% more, but usually need a bachelor's degree.
Keep your credentials active while you train; many hospitals let you switch departments internally.

faq.q: What jobs can former respiratory therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are cardiovascular technologists and technicians (92%), Nuclear Medicine Technologists (81%) and Physical Therapist Assistants (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Medical sonographers are 79% matched and earn $96,590, which is 17% more than the $82,280 respiratory therapist median.

faq.q: Which careers for respiratory therapists pay more?
faq.a: 6 of the 25 matches pay more. Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (79% more), Nuclear Medicine Technologists $101,370 (23% more) and medical sonographers $96,590 (17% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nuclear Monitoring Technicians earn $110,240 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do respiratory therapists need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not a new degree. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than respiratory therapists already have, including all of the top 10. An associate degree is common, held by 63% of workers in the closest match, but imaging needs its own credential.

faq.q: What skills should respiratory therapists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are programming, managing materials, equipment maintenance and managing financial resources. Complex problem solving already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning new imaging equipment is the main step for most moves.
